about: The mutant runner shares the capped-child classifier with proclimit.

mutants.name: gcoom-mutants-text-only
mutants.rule: A capped mutant child's span-queue allocation fault has reason memory.

mutants.name: mutclean-copy-without-git
mutants.rule: The runner's copy carries the checkout's Git file list, so a test that reads the repository (git ls-files) can kill a mutant.

mutants.name: mutclean-other-package-killer-dropped
mutants.from: return Suite{Name: name, Package: "./" + dir, Tags: tags}, nil, true
mutants.rule: A killer in another package of the module (DIR or DIR[TAGS]) is a suite the runner runs, so no row is run by hand.

mutants.name: mutclean-ergo-suite-killer-dropped
mutants.rule: A package ledger's killer named by an ergo suite (lower, std, examples) runs in that suite, with its tools.

mutants.name: mutclean-work-shared
mutants.rule: The default -work is a directory of one run: two runs at once never share coverage counters.

mutants.name: mutclean-work-kept
mutants.rule: The default -work is removed at the end of its run.

mutants.name: xpkg-named-killer-not-run
mutants.rule: A ledger's named killer runs whether or not the coverage pass saw it reach the mutated lines: a test in another package kills through a program it builds.

mutants.name: xpkg-unresolved-skipped
mutants.from: unresolved = append(unresolved, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s: %s", j.Path, m.Name, id))
mutants.rule: A killer whose suite resolves to nothing is refused, not skipped (45 rows named v1:, main:, sched:, tsproj: … and were never run).

mutants.name: xpkg-select-ignored
mutants.rule: Only the selected rows bring killer suites: a run of one row builds the suites that row names, not every killer suite of its ledger.

mutants.name: xpkg-note-kept
mutants.rule: A note after a killer's test name (past a space) is the reader's: the runner runs the test it names.

mutants.name: xpkg-named-dropped
mutants.rule: Every suite records the tests the ledgers name, so a Go suite missing one is refused and a command suite runs a named example that is not a default.

mutants.name: xpkg-example-ledger-own-suite
mutants.rule: A ledger whose directory has no Go tests (an example's, editing .ergo files) brings no suite of its own, which would not build; its named killers judge it.

mutants.name: xpkg-stale-killer-accepted
mutants.rule: A Go suite that lacks a test a ledger names is refused before the mutant pass.
mutants.gap: No runner test builds a suite missing a named test; internal/residue:TestLedgerEditsApplyOnce refuses such a row in the checkout's ledgers before any run (ledger-killer-alias).

mutants.name: xpkg-command-named-dropped
mutants.from:
for _, n := range s.Named {
				if !slices.Contains(names, n) {
mutants.rule: A command suite (the examples) runs a named example that is not a default one.
mutants.gap: The fake module of TestRunnerMatchesModel has Go suites only; the affected run of scripts/examples' ledger (examples:router) exercises it.

mutants.name: b18-nested-killer-from-root
mutants.to: if mod := nestedModule(root, dir); false && mod != "" {
mutants.rule: A killer in a nested Go module (selfhost's hostsyntax) is built in that module; from the checkout's root go test refuses it and the run fails.

mutants.name: b18-nested-package-covered
mutants.rule: A package of a nested module is no -coverpkg package of the checkout: naming it fails every suite's coverage build.

mutants.name: b18-nested-coverdir
mutants.rule: A nested module's suite is built without coverage, so its test binary takes no -test.gocoverdir; with it the killer fails on the unmutated tree and kills nothing.
mutants.gap: No runner test builds a nested module's suite; the affected run of internal/selfhostcheck's ledger (r4-m2.log: hostsyntax:TestFamiliesCoverSyntax failed on the unmutated tree) exercises it.
